title: Understanding the Expression
text: The expression \( \alpha[\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}**{n}(y_i-\sigma(X_{i}\cdot{\theta}**{(t)}))X_i] \) involves several components. Let's break it down:

title: Components of the Expression
text: $$1$$. \( \alpha \) is a scalar (learning rate).\n$$2$$. \( \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}**{n}(y_i-\sigma(X_{i}\cdot{\theta}**{(t)}))X_i \) is a summation over all data points.\n$$3$$. \( $$X_i$$ \) is a vector of length \( $$p$$ \).

title: Dimensions of the Summation
text: The summation \( \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}**{n}(y_i-\sigma(X_{i}\cdot{\theta}**{(t)}))X_i \) results in a vector. Since \( $$X_i$$ \) is a vector of length \( $$p$$ \), the summation also results in a vector of length \( $$p$$ \).
